land.text: the Second Turkic Khaganate's Mongolian heartland: the Basmyls took Ötüken in 744 and 'Later that year a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeats them'; in 745 the Uyghurs killed Kulun Beg, 'the last Göktürk khagan'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Predecessor: Second Turkic Khaganate'. The state has no Cliopatria row of its own and no dossier yet (ia-01-e flagged it); Cliopatria draws its Mongolian land inside the Türgesh row 692-749.

land.text: the Kyrgyz shape of 840, the Orkhon valley and Tuva, after the Kyrgyz 'sacked Ordu-Baliq' in 840

successors.note: Infobox successor. The Yenisei Kyrgyz page says the Kyrgyz 'did not replace them as Mongolia's rulers' after 843, so the steppe beyond the Orkhon is nobody's.

land.text: 'the Uyghurs migrated south and established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in modern Gansu'

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Gansu Uyghur Kingdom'; the page gives no year for the founding (Cliopatria 860).

land.text: the Turfan basin around Gaochang, where the refugees founded the Kingdom of Qocho

successors.note: Infobox successor; no year on the page (Cliopatria 860).

land.text: no land passed: the page lists the Kara-Khanid Khanate as successor and says 'a third group went to seek refuge among the Karluks'

successors.note: Listed because the infobox does; the Karluk country of Zhetysu was never Uyghur direct land in this dossier (see notes).

capitals.name: Ötüken (Orkhon Valley)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Ötüken; Ordu-Baliq later'; the Basmyls took Ötüken in 744 and were driven out later that year. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Karakorum point in the Orkhon Valley; the page gives none.

capitals.name: Ordu-Baliq (Orkhon Valley)
capitals.note: Built under Bayanchur (747-759) on the page's account, no year given, so 748 is the first year after his accession; 'sacked Ordu-Baliq, razing it to the ground' in 840. A second city, Bai Baliq, was built up the Selenga. Coordinates approximate (Orkhon valley).

rulers.name: Qasar (usurper)
rulers.title: usurper
rulers.note: Seized the throne with 20,000 Shatuo horsemen; executed in 840.

rulers.name: Wujie
rulers.note: After the fall: led about 100,000 Uyghurs, invaded Shaanxi in 841, wounded at Shahu in 843, killed in 846. No land is attached to this reign.

rulers.name: Enian
rulers.note: Decisively defeated by the Tang in 847; the page's infobox lists him as last (841-847), its rulers table gives 846-848. No land.

minus.text: the western and northern fringe of the 750 shape that others held in 745-749: Xinjiang (Dzungaria, Turfan-Hami, Tarim: the Tang Beiting protectorate), Tuva (Yenisei Kyrgyz), East Kazakhstan and Almaty (Karluks)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape without its western and northern fringe (Xinjiang, Tuva, East Kazakhstan, Almaty): Mongolia from Shiwei to the Altai and the Gobi, 'the entire territory of the ancient Xiongnu', from 745

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Uyghur shape begins in 750 but the khaganate was established in 744 and 'then reached' Shiwei in the east, the Altai in the west and the Gobi in the south under Kutlug I (744-747), i.e. 'the entire territory of the ancient Xiongnu'. The 750 shape (2.94 M km2) is used for 744-749; the 3.1 M km2 of the infobox is for 800 (ratio 0.95). [fx-23] Now 745-749 and without the fringe. The page dates only the founding at Otuken to 744 ('In 744, the Basmyls captured the Turkic capital of Otuken... Later that year, a Uyghur-Karluk alliance formed against the Basmyls and defeated them') and the killing of Kulun Beg to 745; the ledger (found 744 Orkhon valley, gain 745 Mongolian plateau) already follows that, whereas the keyframe drew the whole 750 shape in 744 (289 cells in the ledger against 12,254: the compiler's snap). The fringe is cut out because the page dates no Uyghur expansion into Dzungaria, Turfan, Tuva or the Tarim before 751 (Turfan after the Tang retreat from Talas, 'the area around Turfan came under the control of the Uighurs'; the Kyrgyz in 758), and the Karluks of East Kazakhstan are a vassal from 746 (ledger), not direct land.

2.94 M km2: the Mongolian plateau (Mongolia 6,434 of 6,490 cells, 2,574 of Inner Mongolia's 5,496), Tuva, and a western fringe in Dzungaria and Turfan-Hami. The page's extent (Shiwei, Altai, Gobi) matches; the footnote says 'the area around Turfan came under the control of the Uighurs' after Talas (751). The infobox gives 3.1 M km2 for 800, ratio 0.95.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 755 shape without Zhetysu, which is vassal (Türgesh and Karluk remnants) and not direct Uyghur land

keyframe_review.note: 755-756: Cliopatria adds 884 cells in Zhetysu (69.5-83 E, 41-46.5 N) to the direct shape. The page says Bayanchur 'brought the Sekiz Oghuz, Kyrgyz, Karluks, Türgesh, Toquz Tatars, Chiks and the remnants of the Basmyls under Uyghur rule' (747-759, no year) and that the Karluks migrated west into Zhetysu; the Karluks page has the Türgesh in Zhetysu until 766. So Zhetysu is drawn as vassal land (events 755 vassal_start, 766 vassal_end), not direct.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 757 shape without Zhetysu (vassal); Dzungaria and Turfan-Hami kept as drawn

keyframe_review.note: 757-762: +1,759 cells (Dzungaria 564 to 1,777 of 1,986 cells, Zhetysu to 1,204, Turfan-Hami to 620, northern Tarim 345, Kyrgyzstan 396). The 751 footnote supports the Turfan side; no page opened dates the Dzungarian or Tarim step (unverified: page budget), so those cells stay. Zhetysu is taken out as in 755.

minus.text: the Kyrgyz country, which 'came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate' in 758 and is a vassal, not direct, land

correction.text: Cliopatria's 763 shape without Zhetysu (Türgesh vassal to 765, Karluks from 766) and without the Kyrgyz country (vassal)

keyframe_review.note: 763-777: +632 cells in the north (51-55 N, 89.6-103.7 E), 585 of them inside Cliopatria's Yenisei Kyrgyz 692 shape, whose own row has a gap 763-792. Yenisei Kyrgyz page: 'In 758, the Uyghurs killed the Kyrgyz khagan and the Kyrgyz came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate'; the Uyghur page: Bayanchur 'destroyed several of their trading outposts before defeating a Kyrgyz army and executing their khan'. Overlordship, so a vassal tint. Zhetysu is again removed (Karluks overran the Türgesh there in 766, Karluks page). Peak 3.89 M km2 in Cliopatria; the infobox 3.1 M (800) is for the later, smaller shape.

minus.text: the Kyrgyz country, which 'came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate' in 758 and is a vassal, not direct, land

correction.text: Cliopatria's 778 shape without Zhetysu and without the Kyrgyz country

keyframe_review.note: 778-782: only 28 Zhetysu cells at Issyk-Kul fewer than 763. Same correction as 763 (Zhetysu and the Kyrgyz country are not direct land).

minus.text: the Kyrgyz country, which 'came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate' in 758 and is a vassal, not direct, land

correction.text: Cliopatria's 783 shape without Zhetysu and without the Kyrgyz country

keyframe_review.note: 783-792: +32 cells around Issyk-Kul and Turfan, noise. Same correction as 763. The page dates no change in 783.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 793 shape plus Turfan-Hami: 'In 792, the Uyghurs ... defeated the Tibetans and Karluks, taking Gaochang'

keyframe_review.note: 793-839, 3.03 M km2 (infobox 3.1 M for 800, ratio 0.98). Cliopatria drops 2,980 cells in 793: Zhetysu (to its Qarlugs row), most of western Dzungaria and the Tianshan, half of Turfan-Hami. The page has the Uyghurs 'taking Gaochang' in 792 (again 803) and defeating Tibetans and Karluks at Beiting in 791, so Turfan-Hami is added back; the western loss fits 'The Karluks ... encroach on Uyghur territory and annexed Futu Valley' (789) and the Altai western limit under Kutlug I. The Kyrgyz country (Cliopatria's own Yenisei Kyrgyz 793 row) stays a vassal to 840.

correction.text: years only: no Uyghur state after 840; 'the Uyghurs migrated south and established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in modern Gansu' and the Kingdom of Qocho near Turfan; the Mongolian plateau is the Kyrgyz Orkhon and stateless steppe

keyframe_review.note: 840-849: the khaganate ended in 840 (infobox 'Disestablished: 840'; 'they sacked Ordu-Baliq, razing it to the ground'). The remnants under Wujie and Enian (841-848) held no known land: they invaded Shaanxi in 841, lost 10,000 at Shahu in 843, Wujie was killed in 846 and Enian defeated in 847. The land is the Kyrgyz Orkhon (Cliopatria's Yenisei Kyrgyz 840 shape), stateless steppe, and the refugee kingdoms of Qocho and Ganzhou.

ledger.note: 744: the Uyghurs and Karluks defeat the Basmyls at Ötüken and found the Uyghur Khaganate. 'In 744, the Basmyls took Ötüken and killed Özmiş Khagan. Later that year a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeats them'; infobox 'Established 744'. The page names Ötüken, not a boundary.

minus.text: the western and northern fringe of the 750 shape that others held in 745-749: Xinjiang (Dzungaria, Turfan-Hami, Tarim: the Tang Beiting protectorate), Tuva (Yenisei Kyrgyz), East Kazakhstan and Almaty (Karluks)

region.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape without its western and northern fringe (Xinjiang, Tuva, East Kazakhstan, Almaty): Mongolia from Shiwei to the Altai and the Gobi, 'the entire territory of the ancient Xiongnu', from 745

ledger.note: 745: the last Göktürk khagan is killed. 'the Uyghurs killed Kulun Beg, the last Göktürk khagan' (745); under Kutlug I the territory reached 'Shiwei ... the Altai Mountains ... the Gobi Desert', 'the entire territory of the ancient Xiongnu'. The page does not say 'the Second Turkic Khaganate fell' in so many words. [fx-23] Region now the keyframe's own shape (Cliopatria's 750 shape without Xinjiang, Tuva, East Kazakhstan and Almaty) instead of the gazetteer's Mongolian Plateau, which differs from the shape by about 3,000 cells each way and made the 750 keyframe remove 2,073 cells; the 745 date and the extent (Shiwei, Altai, Gobi) are the page's, the page dating no expansion into the fringe before 751.

region.text: the Karluk country between the Altai and the eastern shore of Lake Balkhash (Black Irtysh and Tarbagatai)

ledger.note: 746: the Karluk yabghu submits to the Uyghurs. 'Bilge Yabghu Tun Apa Yigen Chor' submitted to the Uyghurs in 746 (died about 753); the Uyghur page lists the Karluks among the peoples brought under Bayanchur's rule. The page gives the tribes' area, not a border.

751: the Tang withdraw after Talas and Turfan passes to the Uyghurs. Footnote: 'the area around Turfan came under the control of the Uighurs, who emerged as the dominant power of Eastern Central Asia'. The page gives no year for the handover; 751 is the footnote's context (Talas). [Review ia-01-f: confidence 1, the footnote gives no year for the Turfan handover (bridging); the Tang example keeps Turfan to c. 790 and this ledger takes Gaochang from Tibet in 792.]

755: Zhetysu under Uyghur overlordship. Bayanchur (747-759) 'brought the Sekiz Oghuz, Kyrgyz, Karluks, Türgesh, Toquz Tatars, Chiks and the remnants of the Basmyls under Uyghur rule'; the page gives no year, 755 is Cliopatria's step into Zhetysu (confidence 1).

region.text: the Kyrgyz country of the upper Yenisei: Tuva and the Minusinsk basin, 'the southern portion of the Minusinsk Hollow'

ledger.note: 758: Bayanchur subdues the Kyrgyz. 'In 758, the Uyghurs turned their attention to the northern Yenisei Kyrgyz. Bayanchur destroyed several of their trading outposts before defeating a Kyrgyz army and executing their khan.' Yenisei Kyrgyz page: 'the Kyrgyz came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate'. Cliopatria draws it as direct land from 763 (Kyrgyz row gap 763-792).

766: the Karluks emerge as an independent khanate under a Yabghu in Zhetysu. The pages give no date for the end of the Uyghur overlordship; 766 ('the Karluk tribes formed a Khanate under the rule of a Yabghu') is a bridging judgement.

766: the Karluks end the Türgesh in Zhetysu. 'In 766, after they overran the Türgesh in Jetisu, the Karluk tribes formed a Khanate under the rule of a Yabghu' and 'occupied Suyab'. The Uyghur page has no Zhetysu entry after Bayanchur; Cliopatria keeps Zhetysu in the Uyghur shape to 792.

region.text: Futu Valley (Fu-tu valley), location not given on the page

ledger.note: 789: the Karluks annex the Futu Valley. 'The Karluks took this opportunity to encroach on Uyghur territory and annexed Futu Valley' (after Külüg's accession in 789). The page gives no location (footnote: Fu-tu valley, Shen-tu Valley in the Xin Tangshu), so the region is a placeholder in Dzungaria where the Karluks page puts them (Tarbagatai).

790: Tibet defeats the Uyghurs and Tang at Tingzhou. 'In 790, the Uyghurs and Tang forces were defeated by Tibetan Empire at Tingzhou.' The page does not say Tingzhou was held after the battle; Beshbalik/Beiting is the gazetteer's name for the place.

792: the Uyghurs take Gaochang. 'In 792, the Uyghurs, led by Qutluq's son Baoyi Qaghan, defeated the Tibetans and Karluks, taking Gaochang.' 791: 'The Tibetans and Karluks suffered another defeat against the Uyghurs at Beiting.' The page repeats 'In 803, the Uyghurs captured Gaochang' without saying it had been lost. [Review ia-01-f: confidence 2, the page names Gaochang, not Hami.]

region.text: Tingzhou, Beiting, Gaochang and Liang Province

ledger.note: 808: last dated Uyghur gain from Tibet. 'In the same year, the Uyghurs seized Liang Province from the Tibetans' (808); later Tibetan moves (816 raid to within two days of Ordu-Baliq, 821 Uyghur counter-attack, 823, 832) changed no ground on the page, and the 821/822 treaty is Sino-Tibetan (Tibetan Empire page). The end year is the page's last ground-changing clash, a bridging judgement.

840: the Kyrgyz throw off the Uyghurs. Yenisei Kyrgyz page: 'In 840 they succeeded in sacking the Uyghur capital, Ordu-Baliq in Mongolia's Orkhon Valley'; Uyghur page: Kulug Bagha 'invited them to invade from the north' with about 80,000 horsemen.

840: Ordu-Baliq falls to the Kyrgyz. The Yenisei Kyrgyz page says they stayed in their homeland after the Tang victory of 843 and did not replace the Uyghurs as Mongolia's rulers, while the Uyghur page has them holding 'the territory from Lake Baikal in the east to the Irtysh River in the west'; Cliopatria gives the Kyrgyz the Orkhon in 840-849.

region.text: the khaganate's last shape: the Mongolian plateau, Tuva and Turfan-Hami

ledger.note: 840: the khaganate falls. 'Disestablished: 840'; 'they sacked Ordu-Baliq, razing it to the ground'; Uyghurs fled in two groups, about 30,000 under Ormïzt to the Tang and about 100,000 under Wujie, a third to the Karluks; 'the Uyghurs migrated south and established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in modern Gansu' and the Kingdom of Qocho (no year). Remnants under Wujie and Enian fought the Tang to 847-848.

wars.name: Uyghur revolt against the Second Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Uyghurs, Karluks and Basmyls rebelled in 742; the Basmyls took Ötüken and killed Özmiş Khagan in 744, then a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeated them and founded the khaganate; Kulun Beg, the last Göktürk khagan, was killed in 745.
wars.note: The Basmyls cease to exist as a people after 744 on the page.

wars.name: Uyghur subjugation of the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Bayanchur destroyed Kyrgyz trading outposts, defeated their army and executed their khan; the Kyrgyz became Uyghur vassals until 840.

wars.name: Uyghur intervention in the An Lushan Rebellion
wars.outcome: About 4,000 Uyghur horsemen helped retake Chang'an and Luoyang in 757 (Luoyang looted for three days); Bögü aided the Tang again at Luoyang in 762. The Tang paid silk and horse-trade prices; no land changed hands.
wars.note: Marriage alliance of 756: Bayanchur married the Tang princess Ningguo.

wars.name: Uyghur-Tibetan wars over the Tarim and Dzungaria
wars.outcome: Tibet beat the Uyghurs and Tang at Tingzhou (790); the Uyghurs beat Tibetans and Karluks at Beiting (791), took Gaochang (792, 803) and seized Liang Province (808); Tibetan attacks of 816, 821, 823 and 832 changed no ground on the page.
wars.note: Tibetan Empire page: 'Tibetans attacked Uyghur territory in 816 and were in turn attacked in 821'; the page opened gives nothing on 790-808.

wars.name: Kyrgyz conquest of the Uyghur Khaganate
wars.outcome: Kulug Bagha, a rival of the usurper Qasar, invited the Kyrgyz; about 80,000 horsemen sacked Ordu-Baliq in 840, Qasar was executed and the khaganate collapsed.
wars.note: Famine and Zhangxin's forced suicide in 839 preceded it (Uyghur page).

wars.name: Tang-Uyghur war of the refugees
wars.outcome: Wujie invaded Shaanxi in 841; Shi Xiong's Tang army killed 10,000 at Shahu on 13 February 843; Wujie was killed in 846 and Enian decisively defeated in 847.
wars.note: No land: the Uyghurs were a refugee host; the Yenisei Kyrgyz page gives the Shahu date as 13 February 843.

certainty.note: A steppe empire: the Shiwei, Altai and Gobi limits are the New Book of Tang's description, not a surveyed line; the western and Tarim frontiers moved with the Tibetan wars (790-808) and are the softest.

sources.title: Uyghur Khaganate

sources.title: Karluks

sources.title: Tibetan Empire
sources.note: 816/821/823 Tibetan-Uyghur attacks and the 821/822 treaty; nothing on 790-808 (page silent).

sources.title: Karluk Yabghu
sources.note: 746 submission of the Karluk yabghu to the Uyghurs; 840 yabghu proclaims himself khagan.

sources.title: Yenisei Kyrgyz
sources.note: 758 Kyrgyz come under the Uyghurs, 840 sack of Ordu-Baliq, 843 Shahu and the refugee kingdoms.

notes:
Pages opened: Uyghur Khaganate (three queries), Karluks, Tibetan Empire, Yenisei Kyrgyz, Karluk Yabghu (5 distinct pages, budget 5). The Second Turkic Khaganate page was not opened (budget): 744-745 rests on the Uyghur page alone.
Founding and end: the dossier uses the infobox, 744 to 840. Cliopatria's row is 750-849: the first six years are a new keyframe (744-749) and 840-849 is marked wrong (remnant Uyghurs under Wujie and Enian held no land; they appear only as rulers 841-848).
Zhetysu: Cliopatria draws Zhetysu (about 1,200 cells) as direct Uyghur land from 755 to 792 and hands it to its Qarlugs row in 793; the Karluks page dates the Karluk Yabghu State in Zhetysu to 766, so the shapes 755-783 are adjusted to drop it and Zhetysu is a vassal tint (Türgesh and Karluks 'brought under Uyghur rule', no year) to 765. The qarlugs dossier (this batch) carries the Karluk side.
Kyrgyz land: 585 cells of Cliopatria's 763 shape are the Yenisei Kyrgyz 692 shape; the Yenisei Kyrgyz dossier (ia-01) records the 763 loss to nobody and the 840 gain from this state.
Dzungaria and the northern Tarim (757-792 additions) are not dated by any page opened; Beshbalik/Tingzhou 790 is a Tibetan win over the Uyghurs and Tang, so the Tang Beiting protectorate probably still held the town (tang-dynasty, ea-04, should carry that). Futu valley (789) has no location on the page.
Pages disagree: the Yenisei Kyrgyz page says the Kyrgyz stayed at home after 843 while the Uyghur page has them holding Baikal to the Irtysh.
Counterpart dossiers needed: second-turkic-khaganate (682-744/745, Orkhon), turgesh exists (ia-01-e), qarlugs written here. Gazetteer: no Ordu-Baliq or Karabalghasun place (capital uses the Karakorum point); no Futu valley. [fx-23, 2026-11-01] The 744 keyframe now starts in 745 (the year the ledger gives the whole Mongolian plateau) and leaves out the Xinjiang, Tuva, East Kazakhstan and Almaty fringe of Cliopatria's 750 shape, which the Uyghur page does not date before 751/758; the 745 gain uses the same shape. Page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uyghur_Khaganate.
